Definition: probably a brier; by implication, a thicket of thorny bushes
BiblicalUsage: Na'atsuts is a thorn or a brier, a thicket of thorny bushes, and it marks places left desolate. In Isaiah 7:19 the thorns and bushes are where the enemy comes to rest in the desolate valleys, and in Isaiah 55:13 the promise is that instead of the thorn shall come up the fir tree, and instead of the brier the myrtle tree.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the brier is the picture of what sin leaves behind, and the myrtle is the picture of what God plants in its place; He does not just clear the thorns; He grows something better where they were.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
